Add SM90 FP8 MMA forward for head dimension 512 (#199)

* Add SM90 FP8 MMA forward for head dimension 512

Signed-off-by: Kate Cheng <yunhsuanc@nvidia.com>

* Harden SM90 FP8 MMA specialization contracts

Signed-off-by: Kate Cheng <yunhsuanc@nvidia.com>

* [Cute,Fwd,Sm90] Load FP8 K with TMA into a two-slot sK

FP8 K went through the single sStage buffer: TMA into sStage, then a
256-thread register copy into sK and a named barrier. sStage and sK have
the same layout, so the copy only moved bytes. It also left a cross-
warpgroup WAR on sK: the next block's copy can overwrite sK while the
other warpgroup's QK WGMMA still reads it. Only an injected delay
triggers it today.

Load K with TMA straight into sK, which now has two slots with their own
TMA pipeline. Each warpgroup waits for its slot, issues QK and releases
the slot after its own QK wait. sStage holds only V, so the V transposes
take their phase from the consumer pipeline state. The slot parity
restarts per tile, so a trace-time assert rejects persistent or CLC
schedulers, which would run several tiles per CTA.

Output is bitwise identical to 8dbd390 on decode, split, MTP, causal and
non-causal prefill, empty-split and sliding-window cases. H200, Gemma 4
TP1 heads: decode b32 16K 842 -> 747 us, prefill 8K causal 6483 ->
6017 us (do_bench); geomean over 14 vLLM-style shapes 0.909x.
Shared memory grows to about 225 of 227 KiB.

Signed-off-by: Simon Veitner <sveitner@redhat.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 8dbc8b84254b514c7a211d5afa57eb4e68028739)
Signed-off-by: yunhsuanc <yunhsuanc@yunhsuanc-dvt-01.nvidia.com>

* [Cute,Fwd,Sm90] Transpose FP8 V between the two QK halves

The V[n-1] transpose was issued after all 32 QK QGMMAs, and a cycle trace
showed it never overlapped them. Issue it between the two Q terms of the
QK sum instead, inside the same commit group, so it runs while the
first 16 QGMMAs execute. _gemm_two_fp8_a and _gemm_qk_fp8_compensated
now name their operands first and second, because the residual term can
also go first.

Output is bitwise identical to the previous commit. H200: decode b32 16K
747 -> 736 us, prefill 8K 6017 -> 5869 us; geomean over 14 shapes
0.896x of 8dbd390.

Signed-off-by: Simon Veitner <sveitner@redhat.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 1ebb85f55df23b022133619156e96b615cfdfbc1)
Signed-off-by: yunhsuanc <yunhsuanc@yunhsuanc-dvt-01.nvidia.com>

* [Cute,Fwd,Sm90] Promote FP8 PV sums to FP32 every KV block

FP8 WGMMA accumulates below FP32 (PTX ISA 9.7.16.5.2). The PV sum of a
whole split stayed in one WGMMA accumulator, so long splits lost mass:
q = 0, V = 1 gave 0.500 at 32K keys and 0.125 at 128K with num_splits=1.
On real Gemma 4 activations at 16K the relative L2 error was 5.5e-2
(layer 5) and 2.3e-1 (layer 59).

Run each block's PV as four 64-column passes into a zero-initialized
32-register scratch, and add the scratch to acc_O with FP32 adds.
Afterwards q = 0, V = 1 gives 1.000 at every length, and layers 5 and 59
reach 3.5e-3 and 2.1e-3. The new test checks the 32K and 128K cases.

After commits 1 and 2 the branch runs at 0.958x of 8dbd390; this commit
alone costs 1.101x because the K copy addresses then spill. On this
commit one fp16-Q case of test_flash_attn_kvcache_fp8_dequant_sm90 misses
its max-error bound by one fp16 ulp (3.17e-3 vs 2.94e-3; 8dbd390 already
reaches 2.93e-3 with num_splits=2). Its error comes from QK, and the
next commit halves it.

Signed-off-by: Simon Veitner <sveitner@redhat.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 3cf312fb12836b9c6b61286df9cf880106e031a7)
Signed-off-by: yunhsuanc <yunhsuanc@yunhsuanc-dvt-01.nvidia.com>

* [Cute,Fwd,Sm90] Issue the residual Q term first in FP8 QK

Each QGMMA truncates its addends relative to the running sum, so the
residual Q terms lose most of their bits when they are added after the
high terms. Issue the 16 residual k-steps first, while the sum is still
small, by passing the residual Q fragment as the first operand. Same
instructions and registers, no measurable time change (0.958x of
8dbd390 after commits 1 to 4, as after commits 1 to 3).

On top of commits 1 to 3: test_flash_attn_fp8_kv_cache.py goes from 10
to 4 failures of 14, real Gemma 4 16K error from 3.5e-3 to 3.0e-3
(layer 5) and 2.1e-3 to 1.7e-3 (layer 59), and the fp16-Q case of
test_flash_attn_kvcache_fp8_dequant_sm90 from 3.174e-3 to 1.465e-3 max
error.

Signed-off-by: Simon Veitner <sveitner@redhat.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 73ff1378309c958106536dfe601ccffe64982f76)
Signed-off-by: yunhsuanc <yunhsuanc@yunhsuanc-dvt-01.nvidia.com>

* [Cute,Fwd,Sm90] Split the FP8 QK sum in causal and local builds

The 4 remaining test_flash_attn_fp8_kv_cache.py failures (logits with
std about 22) come from the QK sum: 32 QGMMAs into one accumulator.
Sum k-steps 0 to 7 into acc_S and 8 to 15 into the PV scratch, which is
idle while QK runs, then wait and add the scratch to acc_S before the
first PV pass. The first block uses its own 32-register temporary.
Both keep the residual-first order of the previous commit.

Only causal and local builds get the split: in non-causal builds ptxas
serializes the WGMMAs (C7511), which ran 1.33 to 2.03x slower. With the
gate, ptxas -v reports no C7511 for causal, local and non-causal builds
(num_splits 1 and 4); without it, the non-causal builds report C7511.

With commits 1 to 5 all 14 tests pass, real Gemma 4 16K error is 1.97e-3
(layer 5) and 1.69e-3 (layer 59), the fp16-Q case of
test_flash_attn_kvcache_fp8_dequant_sm90 drops to 9.8e-4 max error, and
time is 0.982x of 8dbd390 (causal). Non-causal builds keep the accuracy
of the previous commit: the 14 tests made non-causal still fail 4.

Signed-off-by: Simon Veitner <sveitner@redhat.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 3d4be5f852305eac8a36d7b7126f7d85051f3279)
Signed-off-by: yunhsuanc <yunhsuanc@yunhsuanc-dvt-01.nvidia.com>

* [Cute,Fwd,Sm90] Document FP8 MMA accumulation and fp16 Q limits

Comments said the FP8 path accumulates in FP32. FP8 WGMMA sums below
FP32 within an instruction chain (PTX ISA 9.7.16.5.2); only the per-block
PV promotion adds in FP32. State that, state that fp16 Q keeps 8 of its
11 significant bits in the E4M3 pair, and give the real range of the
large-Q test (values up to 896, at most 2.2% error).

Signed-off-by: Simon Veitner <sveitner@redhat.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 322a9af1689fa42b181a729a54dfd8159832939b)
Signed-off-by: yunhsuanc <yunhsuanc@yunhsuanc-dvt-01.nvidia.com>

* [Cute,Fwd,Sm90] Fence sStage reads before releasing it to TMA

The V transpose reads sStage with LDSM (generic proxy), and the next V
tile is written into sStage by TMA (async proxy). The proxy fence ran
after the release, and only lane 0 of each warp arrives on the empty
barrier, so the reads were not ordered before the TMA write (PTX ISA
8.6, 9.7.9.26.2 and 9.7.14.4). Issue the fence and a __syncwarp before
the release. The fence still precedes the per-warpgroup barrier that
makes the transposed sV visible to the PV WGMMA.

No hang or corruption was observed without this; it closes the gap in
the memory model. The release-then-fence order comes from the PR 164
dequant path and 8dbd390 kept it. On its own this commit fixes the V
path only: on 8dbd390 the K copy releases sStage in the same order
until the first commit of this series removes that copy. Output is
bitwise identical to the previous commit and time is unchanged (0.981x
of 8dbd390 for the whole branch).

Signed-off-by: Simon Veitner <sveitner@redhat.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 34337517bfd7a77bc539c0c625a2ae611fe230ca)
Signed-off-by: yunhsuanc <yunhsuanc@yunhsuanc-dvt-01.nvidia.com>

* Format SM90 FP8 forward kernel

Signed-off-by: Kate Cheng <yunhsuanc@nvidia.com>

* [Cute,Fwd,Sm90] Keep the FP8 P tail: scale the P residual in its own PV pass

P = e4m3(256p) + e4m3(256p - hi) rounds both terms to 0 for p below
2^-18 of the running row max, so PV drops those keys while row_sum still
counts them. Blocks run last to first, so a dominant recent key cuts the
earlier context out of the output.

Scale the residual by 32 (|residual| <= 8 for p <= 1, so 256 < 448) and
run it as a second PV pass through the same FP32 scratch, unscaled at
the fold. Keys now reach PV down to 2^-23 of the row max.

Measured on H200 against 6d71c3f:
- Gemma-4 31B FP8, 121K prefill, 10 global layers: per-row error p99
  0.29-0.42% (was 0.86-2.97%; merge base 0.26-0.31%), max 0.48-0.98%
  (was 2.5-7.9%).
- New test_flash_attn_kvcache_fp8_mma_keeps_softmax_tail_sm90 fails
  before (+24%, -100%) and passes after; FP8 suite 41 passed, 2 skipped.
- Kernel time +6% to +13% (prefill 8K x 123K +7%, 2K x 33K +13%,
  decode b64 x 33K +10%, b1 x 123K +6%).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Simon Veitner <sveitner@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Kate Cheng <yunhsuanc@nvidia.com>

* [Cute,Fwd,Sm90] Document the |q| <= 448 range of the FP8 MMA path

Q is quantized as an E4M3 pair at fixed scale 1.0 with no range check.
Measured on H200: rel error 0.2% up to |q| = 448, 2% at 768-896,
15% at 1024, 65% at 2048. Say so where callers look.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Simon Veitner <sveitner@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Kate Cheng <yunhsuanc@nvidia.com>

* [Cute,Fwd,Sm90] Keep the sink LSE for fully masked rows without SplitKV

The empty-split override now runs on every SM90 launch, so a non-split
row with no visible key and a learnable sink returns LSE = -inf instead
of the sink logit. Restrict the LSE override to SplitKV and FP8, as the
merge base did for the non-FP8 path. O is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Simon Veitner <sveitner@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Kate Cheng <yunhsuanc@nvidia.com>

 from quack.cute_dsl_utils import ParamsBase
 from flash_attn.cute.tile_scheduler import (
+    SchedulingMode,
     TileSchedulerArguments,
     SingleTileScheduler,
     SingleTileLPTScheduler,
@@ -66,13 +67,32 @@ def __init__(
             f"Fused quant output not implemented for {type(self).__name__}"
         )

+        # Match the FA3 FP8 path: keep softmax probabilities in registers for PV.
+        # SM90 FP8 needs a different accumulator-to-A-fragment mapping than FP16.
         self.mma_pv_is_rs = mma_pv_is_rs
